categories.name: Core components
categories.description: Explore actuation, sensing, compute and power components for intelligent machines.

children.name: Actuators & motors
children.description: Find integrated joint actuators, servo motors and compact drive assemblies for robotic motion.
children.guidance: Compare continuous and peak torque, speed, thermal limits, voltage and feedback. Match the actuator’s communication interface and mounting to the intended joint.

children.name: Reducers & transmissions
children.description: Explore precision reduction gears and transmissions for robotic joints.
children.guidance: Compare reduction ratio, backlash, stiffness, efficiency and lifetime under the expected load. Check the complete motor-and-gear assembly rather than treating peak gearbox torque as a continuous rating.

children.name: Motor drives & controllers
children.description: Find drive electronics and servo controllers for robotic motors and joints.
children.guidance: Check supported motors, encoder types, current limits and command interfaces. A motor controller is not necessarily an integrated actuator; confirm what hardware is supplied.

children.name: Force & tactile sensing
children.description: Explore force-torque sensors and tactile sensing for contact-aware robotic manipulation.
children.guidance: Match measurement range, resolution, sample rate and mechanical mounting to the contact task. Distinguish whole-wrist force sensing from local fingertip or surface tactile information.

children.name: Vision & range sensing
children.description: Find depth cameras, stereo systems and LiDAR sensors for robot perception.
children.guidance: Compare useful range, field of view, frame rate and performance under the intended lighting. Verify synchronization, calibration and driver support before choosing a camera or range sensor.

children.name: Position & inertial sensing
children.description: Explore encoders, inertial sensors and motion-tracking systems for robotic state estimation.
children.guidance: Check encoder resolution, sensor noise, drift and timing requirements. Distinguish relative motion measurements from absolute pose estimates and confirm the expected reference frame.

children.name: Edge compute
children.description: Find embedded processors and accelerators for on-device robotic perception and control.
children.guidance: Budget power, cooling, memory and I/O before comparing inference performance. Verify supported runtimes and real-time control requirements separately from AI acceleration.

children.name: Power & electronics
children.description: Explore power-conversion, battery and electronic components for robotic systems.
children.guidance: Review voltage, transient current, protection and charging requirements at system level. Battery cells, battery packs and battery-management electronics are separate procurement decisions.

categories.name: Hardware
categories.description: Find robot arms, hands, teleoperation rigs and platforms for development.

children.name: Robot arms
children.description: Explore robot arms and manipulation platforms for development, education and research.
children.guidance: Compare workspace, payload, repeatability, sensing and control interfaces. Check the complete setup, including controller, mounting and end effector, before estimating cost or compatibility.

children.name: Hands & grippers
children.description: Find parallel grippers, adaptive end effectors and dexterous robot hands.
children.guidance: Choose grasp mechanics around the objects and task. Compare opening range, force, tactile feedback and finger control rather than assuming additional fingers guarantee better manipulation.

children.name: Teleoperation rigs
children.description: Explore demonstration-collection hardware and interfaces for controlling robots remotely.
children.guidance: Match leader and follower kinematics, control latency and data synchronization. Check whether the rig records the observations and actions required by the target learning pipeline.

children.name: Research humanoid platforms
children.description: Find humanoid development hardware for embodied AI and locomotion experiments.
children.guidance: Confirm developer access, safety procedures, supported interfaces and replacement-part availability. A humanoid form factor does not establish autonomous capability or suitability for human interaction.

children.name: Mobile bases & rovers
children.description: Explore wheeled, legged and rover development platforms for mobile robotics.
children.guidance: Compare terrain, turning geometry, payload, power and odometry interfaces. Verify braking, emergency-stop behavior and integration requirements for the intended environment.

children.name: DIY & education hardware
children.description: Find buildable robot designs and educational hardware platforms.
children.guidance: Check assembly instructions, bill of materials and design licenses. An open software driver does not establish that the mechanical design is open hardware.

categories.name: Software
categories.description: Explore simulation, learning, navigation, middleware and robot operations software.

children.name: Simulation & physics
children.description: Explore physics engines and simulation platforms for developing and testing robotic systems.
children.guidance: Choose around contact fidelity, sensor rendering, robot assets and compute requirements. Confirm supported versions and licenses before comparing simulation speed or transferring policies to hardware.

children.name: Robot learning frameworks
children.description: Find training workflows for imitation learning, reinforcement learning and robotic policy adaptation.
children.guidance: Check data formats, observation/action interfaces and supported environments. Distinguish a framework’s training infrastructure from the licenses and requirements of individual policies.

children.name: Navigation & SLAM
children.description: Explore mapping, localization, odometry and navigation software for autonomous robots.
children.guidance: Match sensors, coordinate frames and localization assumptions to the deployment environment. Mapping, pose estimation, path planning and obstacle avoidance serve different parts of the navigation stack.

children.name: Motion planning & control
children.description: Find kinematics, dynamics, trajectory-generation and motion-planning tools.
children.guidance: Check robot models, collision representations, timing and control interfaces. A feasible geometric path still needs dynamic and hardware-level validation before execution.

children.name: Middleware & communication
children.description: Explore messaging and dataflow infrastructure for distributed robotic systems.
children.guidance: Compare delivery semantics, timing, transport security and integration requirements. Verify compatibility with the selected ROS distribution or runtime instead of assuming drop-in replacement.

children.name: Perception & geometry
children.description: Find point-cloud processing, calibration and geometric estimation libraries.
children.guidance: Choose tools around sensor modality, calibration assumptions and required geometric outputs. Check numerical precision, runtime requirements and data conventions before connecting pipelines.

children.name: Robot SDKs
children.description: Explore manufacturer and project SDKs for communicating with robotic hardware.
children.guidance: Confirm model, firmware and transport compatibility in the publisher’s documentation. An SDK may expose commands without providing a complete safety or autonomy stack.

children.name: Teleoperation software
children.description: Explore software interfaces and retargeting tools for remotely controlling robots and collecting demonstrations.
children.guidance: Check latency, observation synchronization and supported control devices. Verify robot-side limits and emergency handling before connecting a teleoperation pipeline.

children.name: Visualization & data tools
children.description: Find tools for visualizing, recording and inspecting robotic data.
children.guidance: Check supported message formats, timestamps and playback workflows. Evaluate local versus hosted storage and data-export capabilities before relying on a tool for development records.

children.name: Fleet & autonomy systems
children.description: Explore coordination, operations and autonomy tools for fleets and mobile systems.
children.guidance: Distinguish fleet coordination from onboard autonomy. Review connectivity assumptions, failure handling and operational responsibilities for each supported platform.

categories.name: Models
categories.seo_title: Robot AI models, VLA & world models
categories.description: Find robotic policies, vision-language-action models and perception or world models.

children.name: Vision-language-action
children.description: Explore VLA and robotic foundation-model resources connecting perception, instructions and actions.
children.guidance: Compare observation inputs, action representations, supported embodiments and adaptation requirements. Review model-weight licenses separately from code licenses and benchmark claims.

children.name: Robot policies
children.description: Find imitation-learning and learned-control policies for robotic tasks.
children.guidance: Check how actions are represented and what demonstrations or rewards were used. Assess distribution shift and closed-loop behavior before using a trained policy on a different robot.

children.name: World models
children.description: Explore predictive and generative world-model resources for physical AI and robot planning.
children.guidance: Distinguish generated visual futures from validated physical dynamics. Review conditioning inputs, rollout horizon and evaluation protocols before treating predictions as executable plans.

children.name: Perception models
children.description: Find segmentation, depth, pose and visual representation models for robot perception pipelines.
children.guidance: Check output geometry, coordinate frames and failure cases under the intended camera setup. General image-model performance does not establish task-level robotic reliability.

children.name: Grasping models
children.description: Explore grasp detection and prediction models for robotic manipulation.
children.guidance: Check object representations, gripper geometry and collision assumptions. Evaluate generated grasps with the actual end effector and sensing configuration.

children.name: Language-guided planning
children.description: Find model-based approaches connecting natural-language instructions with robotic skills and plans.
children.guidance: Review grounding, skill interfaces and execution feedback. Language-generated plans require validation against the robot’s capabilities and environment.

categories.name: Datasets
categories.description: Find robotic demonstrations, motion data and scene assets for learning.

children.name: Robot demonstrations
children.description: Find recorded robot interactions and demonstrations for learning manipulation and control.
children.guidance: Inspect robot embodiments, observation/action formats, task diversity and collection procedures. Check train/test splits and dataset licenses before mixing sources.

children.name: Motion & interaction data
children.description: Explore motion capture, egocentric video and human-object interaction datasets relevant to robotics.
children.guidance: Assess modality, coordinate systems, consent and licensing. Human motion and video may require retargeting or additional supervision before they can train robot actions.

children.name: Scene & object assets
children.description: Find 3D scenes and object resources for robotics perception and simulation.
children.guidance: Check geometry, scale, physical annotations and asset licenses. A visual mesh may need collision geometry and dynamics parameters before it works in simulation.

categories.name: Benchmarks
categories.description: Explore tasks and evaluation suites for manipulation, navigation and control.

children.name: Manipulation
children.description: Explore task suites for evaluating grasping, manipulation and language-conditioned robotic behavior.
children.guidance: Compare task definitions, robot configuration, evaluation splits and success criteria. Do not compare scores from different environment versions as if they measure identical performance.

children.name: Navigation & embodied interaction
children.description: Find evaluation tasks for navigation and interaction in embodied environments.
children.guidance: Inspect observations, maps, instructions and permitted agent actions. Check how task success and path efficiency are measured and whether test environments overlap with training data.

children.name: Locomotion & whole-body control
children.description: Explore evaluation environments for locomotion, humanoid skills and motor-control research.
children.guidance: Review body models, contact assumptions, control frequency and reward or metric definitions. Simulation task completion does not establish real-hardware robustness.

children.name: Policy evaluation
children.description: Find tools and protocols for evaluating robotic policies and generalization.
children.guidance: Review task coverage, sample counts, seeds and evaluation conditions. Reproduction in simulation and performance on physical hardware provide different kinds of evidence.

categories.name: Companies
categories.description: Find robotics manufacturers, AI developers and automation companies.

children.name: Humanoid developers
children.description: Discover organizations developing humanoid robotic platforms and related systems.
children.guidance: Distinguish prototypes, development hardware and products with documented deployment support. Verify current platform status and published interfaces with the organization.

children.name: Manipulation & arm makers
children.description: Find companies developing robotic arms, end effectors and manipulation platforms.
children.guidance: Review the manufacturer’s platform families and supported integration ecosystem. A company profile is not a claim that every product supports a particular controller or research stack.

children.name: Mobile & legged robot makers
children.description: Find developers of wheeled, quadruped and other mobile robotic platforms.
children.guidance: Compare stated operating environments, integration support and service arrangements. Mobility form, intended application and autonomous capability should be evaluated separately.

children.name: Industrial automation
children.description: Discover robot manufacturers and automation companies serving industrial workflows.
children.guidance: Review the specific robot family, integrator support and intended process. Company-level inclusion does not certify a work cell’s safety or compliance.

children.name: Service & logistics robotics
children.description: Find organizations building service and logistics robotic systems.
children.guidance: Review intended users, deployment conditions and operational support. A robot used inside a factory or hospital may serve logistics rather than manufacturing or medical treatment.

children.name: AI & robotics software
children.description: Discover developers of robotic intelligence, spatial models and software infrastructure.
children.guidance: Separate research demonstrations from supported products. Verify model access, software interfaces, licensing and deployment commitments with each organization.

children.name: Component suppliers
children.description: Find suppliers of actuation, sensing and robot-development components.
children.guidance: Use product-level documentation to establish specifications and availability. A supplier’s broad catalogue does not guarantee suitability for a particular robotic application.

categories.name: Products
categories.description: Explore complete robots by form and platform; confirm availability with the maker.

children.name: Humanoid & biped robots
children.description: Explore humanoid and bipedal robot platforms, from research projects to manufacturer product lines.
children.guidance: Bipedal locomotion and humanoid form are related but distinct properties. Check the exact body design, developer interfaces, operating limits and availability; two legs do not establish human-like capability.

children.name: Quadruped robots
children.description: Explore four-legged robot platforms for research, development and inspection.
children.guidance: Check terrain, operating limits, payload support and developer interfaces. Confirm the exact edition and service requirements with the maker.

children.name: Mobile manipulators
children.description: Find robot platforms combining a mobile base with manipulation capability.
children.guidance: Assess reach, payload, stability and navigation assumptions together. Confirm how base and arm interfaces coordinate and what safety procedures the publisher requires.

children.name: Mobile robots & rovers
children.description: Explore wheeled and rover robotic platforms for autonomy and development.
children.guidance: Check terrain, drive geometry, localization and payload requirements. Distinguish onboard autonomy from remote operation and platform-level developer tools.

children.name: Consumer & education robots
children.description: Discover programmable and educational robot products for learning and home projects.
children.guidance: Check intended users, assembly needs, supported programming environments and maintenance. Confirm age guidance and supervision requirements with the publisher.

children.name: Aerial & marine robots
children.description: Explore flying and underwater robotic platforms and development ecosystems.
children.guidance: Review operating environment, communication, propulsion and failure handling. Air and water impose different platform requirements; check applicable operating rules for the planned use.

children.name: Industrial arm systems
children.description: Explore complete arm systems for industrial and collaborative automation workflows.
children.guidance: Compare workspace, payload and integration support for the specific model. Collaborative operation depends on the complete application and risk assessment, not the arm label alone.

categories.name: Research & learning
categories.description: Explore robotics labs, learning materials, official documentation and references.

children.name: Academic labs
children.description: Discover university labs studying robot learning, perception, control and human-robot interaction.
children.guidance: Use current lab pages to identify research themes and original publications. Lab inclusion is not a claim about recruitment, collaboration availability or commercial products.

children.name: Research institutes
children.description: Find research organizations contributing to robotic intelligence and intelligent machines.
children.guidance: Review original project pages and publication dates. Separate research programs, public artifacts and supported technology offerings.

children.name: Courses & documentation
children.description: Explore robotics learning materials and publisher-maintained documentation.
children.guidance: Check prerequisites, supported versions and whether material is conceptual or platform-specific. Use official release documentation when implementing a hardware workflow.

children.name: Standards & reference collections
children.description: Find official robotics terminology, industry references and curated discovery collections.
children.guidance: Distinguish formal published standards from drafts, association practices and community lists. A directory informed by a standard is not itself certified against that standard.
